descriptionChirho: Physical contact or touching of a person, object, or sacred item in the Qal stem, covering general tactile contact, prohibited/taboo touch (do not touch), and ritual contact contexts; Arabic لَمَسَ/يَلْمِسُ/مَسَّ, Korean 만지다, Swahili -gusa, Hindi छूना, Spanish tocar.

Reaching a destination, arriving at a place, or extending to a point — includes both Qal occurrences with 'reach' semantics and intransitive Hifil; Arabic بَلَغَ/وَصَلَ/يَصِلُ/حَلَّ, Korean 닿다/이르다/도달하다/도착하다, Swahili -fika/-fikia, Hindi पहुँचना/आना, Spanish llegar/alcanzar.

labelChirho: cause to reach, bring upon (Hifil causative)
descriptionChirho: Causative Hifil: causing something to reach, arrive at, or come upon a target — making something touch or bringing it down to someone; Arabic أَوْصَلَ/يُوصِلُ, Korean 닿게 하다, Hindi पहुंचाना, Spanish hacer llegar/hacer tocar, Swahili -fikisha.

Striking or afflicting someone, often with divine agency — Piel intensive stem and Qal occurrences where cross-linguistic evidence shows striking rather than mere touching; Arabic ضَرَبَ, Korean 치다, Swahili -piga, Hindi मारना, Spanish herir/golpear.

Passive of striking: being stricken, smitten, defeated, or afflicted — Nifal reflexive-passive, Pual intensive passive, and Qal passive participle; Arabic انهَزَمَ/مَضْرُوب/يُصابونَ, Korean 패하다/당하다, Swahili -pigwa/-adhibiwa, Hindi मारा हुआ/पीड़ित, Spanish azotado/herido/afligido.

Specialized Hifil usage: extending property boundaries to adjoin or annex, joining field to field — a distinct metaphorical extension of 'reaching' applied to land tenure; Arabic يُلحِقُونَ (those who attach), Korean 연결하다 (connect), Swahili -unganisha (unite), Hindi जोड़ना (join), Spanish juntar (join).
